findings.description: The add-receiver options and the removal checkboxes show platform and use client_id only when platform is absent. Platform is optional deployment text, and seeding rejects duplicate client IDs but not duplicate platforms. Two registered media clients with the same platform, such as a requesting agent and a separate receiver on one platform, therefore appear identically. The owner cannot tell which service is being approved or removed, although approval is specific to one receiving service (FR-020). Selecting the wrong option would grant the other service photos and clips, or leave the intended service approved. Show the client_id beside the platform, at least when labels collide, or require unique labels for media clients.
findings.title: Camera approvals identify services only by a non-unique platform label

summary: Risk-based inspection of the event-media handoff: staging and cleanup, grants, approvals, withdrawal between reads, receiver download and audit, the MCP sharing tool and media-only scope gating, admin camera settings and delete-now, event writing and delivery, migrations, storage infrastructure, and the official-API pilot. No blocking or major defect was established. One minor receiver-identification issue is reported. Tasks the plan records as planned or in-progress (including the production event media source, direct frame/clip capture and full event filters) were not treated as defects. The controller evidence contains only one command, governance validation, which exited 0 with its output suppressed; it supplies no unit, integration, build or lint results for this digest, and this review ran none. Live Ring, Azure SQL and Blob behavior was inspected in code only.
